name: Tallinn Zoo
description: Estonia's only zoo has wide paved paths that work well with a stroller and plenty of big animals for a toddler to point at. In winter the indoor exhibitions and the Children's Zoo barn give you warm breaks between outdoor loops.
tips: Pre-school children get in free with the paying adult, so a toddler visit costs only the adult or family ticket.

price.note: Oct–Apr gate prices; online EUR 1 cheaper. Summer (May–Sep): adult 19, family 38. Pre-school children free with the adult who bought the ticket; family ticket = up to 2 adults + children up to 19.

discounts: Family ticket (2 adults + children up to 19)
Free entry for under-19s on Children's Saturdays (2nd Saturday, Nov-Apr; check dates)
Combined family ticket with Open Air Museum
hours: Daily 9:00-17:00 in winter (ticket office until 16:00); indoor exhibitions Mon 11:00-16:00, Tue-Sun 10:00-16:00; hours change by season

parkingInfo.note: Free parking at the North Entrance (Paldiski mnt 145). The West Entrance car park (Ehitajate tee 150) is paid, using a parking card validated at the ticket office or by a traffic warden. Free for visitors with a disability parking card. Fills up on weekends and holidays, so arrive early.

photos.credit: The original uploader was Kristjans at Estonian Wikipedia. · CC BY-SA 3.0

name: Children's Zoo at Tallinn Zoo
description: A small farm-animal corner inside the zoo, with goats and other domestic animals at toddler eye level. In winter the animals live in a barn you can walk through, so it still works on cold days.
tips: The barn is closed on the last Monday of each month for cleaning, and the goat yard shuts in bad or very cold weather.

price.note: Included in the Tallinn Zoo ticket (Oct–Apr gate prices; summer adult 19, family 38). Pre-school children free with a paying adult.

hours: Daily 10:00-17:00 (barn); closed last Monday of the month

parkingInfo.note: Inside Tallinn Zoo, so the zoo's parking applies: free at the North Entrance (Paldiski mnt 145), paid with a validated card at the West Entrance (Ehitajate tee 150).

name: Children's Museum Miiamilla
description: A hands-on children's museum in Kadriorg Park with role-play rooms and things to touch, open, and climb. It's aimed mostly at preschoolers, but a confident walker will find plenty to do too.
tips: You need a time-slot ticket for everyone, including free babies, and on weekends tickets are sold only online in advance.

price.note: Child EUR 6 from age 3; under-2s free but still need a booked ticket. Family = up to 2 adults + children under 19. Visits capped at 2 hours. City museum page says under-3s are free, so the cut-off is unclear.

discounts: Free with Tallinn Card (booking still needed)
hours: Sep-May: Tue-Fri 12:00-18:00, Sat-Sun 10:00-17:00; Jun-Aug: Tue-Sun 10:00-17:00; closed Mon

parkingInfo.note: No parking on L. Koidula street itself. Visit Estonia sends drivers to the car parks by Kumu and Kadriorg Stadium. Kumu says its lots on Valge and Mäekalda streets are free (a few minutes' walk). The Kadriorg Stadium area appears to be in the Kesklinn paid zone.

name: Seaplane Harbour (Lennusadam)
description: A huge maritime museum in old seaplane hangars, with a real submarine, boats, and lots of open floor for a toddler to wander. Outside you can visit the Suur Tõll icebreaker on the same ticket.
tips: Food and drink can't be brought inside, so plan snacks before or after.

price.note: Combined ticket (Hangar, exhibition, Suur Tõll, Valvas): adult €22, child (8–18) €11, family €40. Children under 8 free. Seaplane Harbour + Fat Margaret combo €30/€15/€60; museum ships only €12/€6/€15.

discounts: Seaplane Harbour + Fat Margaret combined ticket
hours: Oct-Apr: Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00; May-Sep: daily 10:00-19:00; ticket sales end 30 min before closing

parkingInfo.note: Free for museum visitors in the designated lot across Vesilennuki street. You must register the car on the screen near the self-service terminals or at the cloakroom. Other spaces nearby (e.g. right of the building) are paid by app according to third-party reports.

name: Kumu Art Museum
description: Estonia's main art museum is a big, airy modern building where a toddler can look at colourful works while you have a quieter, warm outing. It runs family programmes, but those are aimed at 4-8 year olds, so with a 1-2 year old treat it as a slow stroll.
tips: The family ticket allows one visit within a year of purchase, so you can buy it ahead and go on a bad-weather day.

price.note: Discount ticket EUR 11 (students, seniors 65+, pupils). Family = up to 2 adults + their underage children. Free age for small children not confirmed; some exhibitions/films are free entry.

hours: Tue, Thu-Sun 10:00-18:00; Wed 10:00-20:00; closed Mon (check seasonal changes)

parkingInfo.note: Free parking next to the museum on Valge street ('Kumu Parking' on Google Maps) and on Mäekalda street. Accessible spaces are on Mäekalda.

photos.credit: Jean-Pierre Dalbéra from Paris, France · CC BY 2.0
Jean-Pierre Dalbéra from Paris, France · CC BY 2.0
Jean-Pierre Dalbéra from Paris, France · CC BY 2.0
Jean-Pierre Dalbéra from Paris, France · CC BY 2.0

name: Kadriorg Park
description: Tallinn's grandest park has paved paths for strollers, the Swan Pond, and flower gardens that are nice for a slow walk with a napping baby. Cafés, toilets, and playgrounds are spread around the park, so it's easy to stay for half a day.
tips: Pair a park walk with Miiamilla or Kumu on the same trip, as all three are a few minutes apart.

price.note: Park entry is free.

parkingInfo.note: Free: the Kumu lots on Valge and Mäekalda streets at the upper end of the park. Paid: the Kadriorg Stadium area, where the stadium site quotes Kesklinn-zone rates (€0.025/min Mon–Fri 7–19, Sat 8–15, Sun free), and private lots such as Koidula 38 (P88, about €1.20/h). There is also a lot behind the Mikkel Museum on Weizenbergi, fee unknown. Pargi.ee should work in the municipal zone; private lots were not checked.

name: Kadriorg Children's Park playground
address: Next to Lydia Koidula 21c (Miiamilla), Kadriorg, Tallinn
description: A large historic playground beside the Miiamilla museum, with a sandy area where little ones can dig and a famous old blue slide. It's one of the playgrounds most often recommended for the smallest children.
tips: Bring sand toys; the city plans a rebuild (finish targeted for summer 2028), so check for short closures.

price.note: Free public playground.

parkingInfo.note: No dedicated parking. Use the Kadriorg Park options: the free Kumu lots (Valge/Mäekalda) or paid lots and street parking near Weizenbergi and Koidula. Which zone covers the exact spot was not confirmed.

name: Tallinn Botanic Garden
description: Big outdoor gardens and forest paths for summer, plus a warm Palm House and greenhouses that make a good winter outing with a toddler. Paths are mostly calm and spacious, with picnic areas for snack breaks.
tips: The Palm House is closed on the last Monday of each month.

price.note: Discount (pupils, students, pensioners) €5; family = up to 2 adults + children up to 19 €16; Family Card holders €9; e-discount ticket from €4.50. Free age for toddlers not stated.

hours: Winter (Oct-Apr): outdoor gardens 9:00-20:00, greenhouses/Palm House 11:00-16:00, visitor centre 10:00-16:00

parkingInfo.note: Has a large car park at Kloostrimetsa tee 52, next to the Palm House/Winter Garden. No source said whether it is free. It is outside the municipal paid zones, so it is likely free, but that is unverified.

photos.credit: Raita Futo from Tokyo, Japan · CC BY 2.0

name: Pirita Beach
description: Tallinn's longest sandy beach has children's playgrounds, changing cabins, and lifeguards in summer. The shallow sand is great for a toddler with a bucket and spade, and the pine woods behind it give shade.
tips: Lifeguards are on duty in summer 9:00-20:00 on weekdays and 9:00-21:00 at weekends, so pick those hours for paddling.

price.note: Free public beach.

hours: Open all the time; lifeguards in summer

parkingInfo.note: The Pirita municipal zone covers the Merivälja tee 1c and 1e car parks. Paid only 15 May–15 Sep, 10:00–22:00, at €0.01/min (€0.60/h), with the first 15 minutes free. Free the rest of the year, so free on today's date (October). Gets very busy on hot summer days.

photos.credit: Guillaume Speurt from Vilnius, Lithuania · CC BY-SA 2.0
Guillaume Speurt from Vilnius, Lithuania · CC BY-SA 2.0
Guillaume Speurt from Vilnius, Lithuania · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Stroomi Beach Park
description: A locals' beach in northern Tallinn with shallow water, a playground, and long paved paths for strollers. Outdoor cafés and an ice-cream truck in summer make it easy to stay a while.
tips: Water quality is said to be a bit lower than at Pirita, so check the city's bathing water notices before swimming.

price.note: Free public beach.

parkingInfo.note: ERR reported free parking at Stroomi (and Pikakari) beaches. That source is from around 2020, so confirm before relying on it.

photos.credit: Vicky Brock from Tallinn, UK · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Toompark and Snelli Pond
description: A green park right under the Old Town walls, built around the last surviving piece of the old moat. It's a short, flat loop with ducks to watch, ideal for a quick stroller walk between city errands.
tips: In winter the pond is a popular skating spot, which toddlers love to watch from the path.

price.note: Free public park.

parkingInfo.note: Street parking only. Toompuiestee and Kaarli pst form part of the Südalinn zone boundary (€0.08/min, 24/7). Nearby streets on the outer side may be Kesklinn (€0.025/min, weekday/Saturday hours). The first 15 minutes are free with a parking clock. Check the exact street on the city's zone map.

name: Löwenruh Park
description: A four-hectare park around a round pond with several playgrounds, including one built to be accessible. Visitors describe a big play structure with options for different ages, plus easy paths for strollers.

price.note: Free public park.

parkingInfo.note: No parking information found. The park is in Kristiine, which appears to be outside the municipal paid zones, so nearby street parking is probably free. Unverified.

name: Kalamaja Park
description: A former cemetery turned into a leafy local park in the Kalamaja neighbourhood, popular with families for a quiet walk. It's a handy stop if you're spending the day in Kalamaja or at the Seaplane Harbour.

price.note: Free public park.

parkingInfo.note: Street parking only. The city extended the paid area over most of Kalamaja, and the Kesklinn zone boundary runs along Kopli/Telliskivi streets. Likely Kesklinn rates: €0.025/min Mon–Fri 7–19, Sat 8–15, free on Sundays. The exact boundary near the park is unconfirmed.

name: Estonian Open Air Museum and Farm Kid's World
description: A big seaside park of old farmhouses, windmills, and forest paths, with Farm Kid's World offering domestic animals and an outdoor adventure trail for small children. It's a full day out with lots of space for a toddler to explore.
tips: Children up to 8 get in free, and Farm Kid's World is only open Thursday to Sunday in winter.

price.note: Winter season prices: single €14, reduced €10, family €30 (up to 2 adults + children up to 19), evening ticket from 16:00 €7 (family €15). Summer €18 / €12 / €38. Children up to 8 free.

discounts: Combined family ticket with Tallinn Zoo (EUR 40 winter, EUR 55 summer)
hours: Winter: Tue-Sun, park 10:00-19:00, buildings 10:00-17:00; Farm Kid's World Thu-Sun 10:00-16:00

parkingInfo.note: Free parking for museum visitors at Vabaõhumuuseumi tee 12.

photos.credit: dalbera from Paris, France · CC BY 2.0
dalbera from Paris, France · CC BY 2.0

name: Tallinn Central Library, Südalinna branch
description: The central library's main building has a parent-and-baby room with a changing table, sink, and armchair for feeding, which makes it a calm city-centre stop with a little one. Children up to 7 can get a free library card under the 'Born to Be a Reader' programme.
tips: Ask about the free library card for children under 7, which comes with a keepsake card pocket.

price.note: Free entry and free library sessions; registration may be needed when places are limited.

discounts: Free library card for children up to 7

parkingInfo.note: No library car park found. Estonia pst is in the downtown core; the city lists Estonia pst 7 as a Südalinn location. Likely €0.08/min (€4.80/h), paid 24/7, first 15 minutes free with a parking clock.

name: Kalamaja Library toddler mornings
description: A small neighbourhood library that has run 'põnnihommik' (toddler mornings) with stories and play for 2-5 year olds and their parents. It's free, gentle, and a nice way to meet other local families.
tips: The latest library page says the sessions were paused and would return in autumn, so call 683 0970 or email kalamaja@tln.lib.ee to check dates and registration.

price.note: Free entry and free library sessions; registration may be needed when places are limited.

parkingInfo.note: Street parking in Kalamaja, which is likely in the Kesklinn zone (€0.025/min Mon–Fri 7–19, Sat 8–15, free on Sundays). Weekday-morning events fall in paid hours. Library address and zone not verified.

name: Estonian Children's Literature Centre
description: An Old Town house full of children's books, illustration galleries, and a fairytale attic on the top floor where kids can play and read. It runs toddler sessions and Saturday family mornings, so it's a cosy winter option.
tips: Groups and special sessions should be booked ahead by phone.

price.note: Entry policy for regular visits not confirmed.

hours: Weekdays 10:00-18:00, Sat 11:00-16:00 (autumn schedule from a third-party listing)

parkingInfo.note: Pikk 73 is at the north end of the Old Town, so it is likely in the Vanalinn zone: €0.10/min (€6/h), paid 24/7, very few spaces. Cheaper Kesklinn-zone streets are just outside the walls. Unverified.

name: Mängu Saar Playroom
address: Päevalille tn 4, Tallinn (also Kopli tn 25 and Osmussaare tn 8)
description: A calm, Montessori-inspired indoor playroom with climbing areas and role-play corners that suits younger children better than big trampoline parks. Parents get seating where they can watch, and there's a small snack corner.
tips: You must buy a digital ticket for a time slot in advance, so don't just turn up.

price.note: Price not confirmed; prepaid digital ticket required.

parkingInfo.note: The Haabersti location is at Päevalille tn 4 (other branches are at Kopli 25 and Osmussaare 8). No parking information found. It is outside the municipal paid zones, so residential street parking is probably free. Unverified.

name: Super Skypark (T1 Mall)
address: Peterburi tee 2, T1 Mall of Tallinn
description: A big trampoline and play centre on the top floor of T1 Mall, with a separate toddler area of mini trampolines and swings. It's loud and busy at peak times, so weekday mornings are best with a 1-2 year old.
tips: Children aged 7 and under must be supervised by a parent the whole time.

price.note: Child day passes reported from EUR 11 (third-party, unconfirmed); under-3 price not confirmed.

discounts: Tallinn Card discount (also for up to 2 children aged 0-6 with an adult card holder)

parkingInfo.note: T1 underground car park and garage: first 4 hours free, recorded by number-plate cameras with no clock needed. After that €0.75 per 30 min, €6 per 24h. Pay by EuroPark app, pargi.ee, ParkMan or SMS 1902. The underground garage is open 07:00–23:00. Height limit 2.4 m underground and 2.3 m in the garage.

name: Lohesaba Adventure City
description: An indoor play centre with a separate soft-play and developmental-games area for the smallest children. Adults get in free, which keeps a rainy-day visit cheap.
tips: No booking is needed for normal play visits.

price.note: Adults free; child price not confirmed.

parkingInfo.note: The address is Mustamäe tee 50 (Kristiine). No parking information found.

name: Kalev Spa Water Park
description: A city-centre water park with a small children's pool with attractions, kids' slides, and a separate training pool, a good warm option in winter. It's walkable from the Old Town, so it's easy to combine with other plans.
tips: Go on a weekday, when the family pass is cheaper than at weekends.

price.note: Day ticket for children aged 1–6 €6.80; family pass €68 weekday / €83 weekend (2 adults + up to 3 children). The price list also shows unlabelled day tickets of €24/€28 and €23 – adult price not confirmed from labels.

parkingInfo.note: The lot in front of the water park is in the Old Town (Vanalinn) zone: €0.10/min, pay with pargi.ee or the EuroPark app. 11 EuroPark spots there are free with a pass from the Kalev Spa checkout, displayed in the car. Discounted parking for guests at Väike-Rannavärava 6: €5 for 3 h, added to the water park bill (give your plate number). The source is from March 2023, so confirm before relying on it.

name: Ülemiste Centre
description: A large shopping centre with mother-and-baby rooms, free stroller hire, and the Lennumaa play area for small children. It's a practical rainy-day stop where you can run errands and let a toddler burn off energy.
tips: Parking is free for 5 hours, and there are wider family spaces near the entrance.

price.note: Free entry; play centres inside are paid separately.

parkingInfo.note: 5 hours free in the outdoor lot, garage and underground car park, tracked by plate cameras with no clock needed. After that €1 per started 30 min, €12 per 24h. Start paid time yourself with pargi.ee, SMS or Snabb. The outdoor lot is open 24h; the garage and underground car park 08:00–00:00.

name: Rätsepa Farm Animal Park
description: A farm west of Tallinn with goats, sheep, rabbits, poultry, and more unusual animals like kangaroos and ostriches, most of which you can pet. A guide introduces the animals, which toddlers usually love.
tips: Visits are by advance booking only, so contact info@ratsepa.ee or +372 529 9849 first.

price.note: Price not confirmed.

parkingInfo.note: A rural farm in Harju-Risti, about 30 minutes' drive from Tallinn. The listing shows free parking.

name: MaryMaris Family Entertainment Centre
address: Paldiski mnt 102, 2nd floor, Rocca al Mare Centre, Tallinn
description: A big new play centre, more than 1,500 m², that opened on the 2nd floor of Rocca al Mare in January 2026. It has ball pits, slides, trampolines and labyrinths, plus a separate toddler zone where under-3s are away from the big kids.
tips: One adult per child gets in free, so one parent per toddler pays nothing extra.

price.note: Child ticket €15 Mon–Thu, €17 Fri–Sun and holidays; under-1s €7. One accompanying adult per child free; extra adult €2. Large-family/special-needs child €11 Mon–Thu.

parkingInfo.note: First 2 h per day free (all sessions added up); then €1 per 30 min, start paid parking in Snabb, Pargi.ee or SMS 1902. 'Convenience parking' bays by the main entrance are paid from the first minute. ERR reports children's play-area visitors can get 3-4 h free by registering with the play area. Zone shown as X9 on one part of the mall page and X122 on another, so check the sign.

name: Seiklusmaa Rocca al Mare
address: Paldiski mnt 102, 2nd floor, Rocca al Mare Centre, Tallinn
description: A play centre with a two-storey climbing frame, slides, a ball area and a role-play zone. A separate climbing area for toddlers keeps little ones off the big structure.
tips: Parents of under-4s have to stay with them; children 4 and over may play on their own.

price.note: Unconfirmed for this location: Järve list shows €8.90/30 min, €10/1 h, €12/2 h, €14.90 day ticket, accompanying adult €2.

discounts: 15% off play time with Perekaart (family card)

parkingInfo.note: First 2 h per day free (all sessions added up); then €1 per 30 min, start paid parking in Snabb, Pargi.ee or SMS 1902. 'Convenience parking' bays by the main entrance are paid from the first minute. ERR reports children's play-area visitors can get 3-4 h free by registering with the play area. Zone shown as X9 on one part of the mall page and X122 on another, so check the sign.

name: Seiklusmaa Järve
address: Pärnu mnt 238, 2nd floor, Järve Keskus, Tallinn
description: A play centre inside Järve Keskus with monkey bars, a three-lane wave slide, a ball pit, a trampoline and a separate climbing area for toddlers. Good for rainy days, and the mall's 5 free parking hours give you plenty of time.
tips: Under-4s need a parent with them the whole time; an accompanying adult ticket is only €2.

price.note: Per visit: €8.90 for 30 min, €10 for 1 h, €12 for 2 h, €14.90 day ticket, 5 day tickets €55; overtime €7/h. Accompanying adult €2. Groups: 1 h €6, 2 h €8, day €10.

parkingInfo.note: First 5 h free; after that €0.75 per 30 min via Snabb, Pargi.ee or SMS (zone X23). Underground garage open 08:00-23:00.

name: Meie Mängumaa Playroom (Haabersti)
address: Meistri 22, Tallinn (second room at Osmussaare 8, Lasnamäe)
description: A 270 m² party playroom for children aged 1-12 that also holds open 'play days' with day tickets. It's quieter than the mall play centres, which suits toddlers who get overwhelmed easily.
tips: Day tickets are sold online only and every person in the room needs one; check the website for this week's play-day dates.

price.note: Day ticket bought online for each child and adult; price not confirmed.

hours: Play days vary week to week (e.g. 10:00-21:00); check the website

name: TikiTaka Playroom
address: Kadaka tee 42b, 2nd floor (Kadaka Trade Center), Tallinn
description: A small private playroom in Mustamäe, mostly rented for birthday parties. On Wednesdays it opens for free play without booking.
tips: Go on a Wednesday between 10:00 and 15:00; take the lift to the 2nd floor and turn left.

price.note: Official site lists only private playroom bookings per time slot (€59–€139 depending on day and slot); per-person entry price not shown.

hours: Open free play Wed 10:00-15:00 (unless booked); parties 10:00-21:00

parkingInfo.note: Free parking beside the building.

name: Miniland Playroom
description: A long-running playroom that welcomes drop-in visits on weekdays as well as birthday parties. Babies under one play free, so it works well for siblings of different ages.
tips: Under-3s must have an adult with them; check Facebook for this week's opening hours first.

price.note: Per child, by time: 1 h €6, 2 h €8, 3 h €9 (day ticket), from age 1. Adult price not stated.

name: Trampolino Trampoline Centre
description: A trampoline centre in Ülemiste that mainly caters to children aged 7 and up, but toddlers can come with a parent. It's best for confident 2-year-olds who love bouncing, not for crawlers.
tips: Under-7s need a companion aged 16 or older with them.

price.note: Toddler (up to 4) €8.50; standard ticket €11.50 Mon–Thu / €14.90 Fri–Sun & holidays; accompanying adult €2; socks €3.50.

parkingInfo.note: Ülemiste centre parking: 5 h free (see existing ulemiste-centre entry).

name: PlayDate Play Studio
address: Kallaste tn 7, A-building 2nd floor (Tabasalu Keskus), Tabasalu, Harku vald
description: A small play studio for children under 6, a short drive west of Tallinn, with regular open play sessions and baby parties. It's calmer and more baby-focused than the big play centres.
tips: Register for an 'Avatud mänguaeg' (open play) slot online; there is a lift.

price.note: Private play studio hire for your group only: 3 h from €110 (no per-person entry).

hours: Mon-Sun 9:00-21:00 by booking; open play at set times

name: Rocca al Mare Shopping Centre
description: One of Estonia's biggest malls, with more than 170 shops, a large food court and two paid play centres (MaryMaris and Seiklusmaa) on the 2nd floor. On a rainy day you can run errands and let a toddler play in one trip.
tips: Since 1 July 2026 only 2 h per day are free, so start paid parking in the app if you combine shopping with a play centre, or ask the play area to register your extra free time.

price.note: Free entry; play centres inside are paid separately.

parkingInfo.note: First 2 h per day free (all sessions added up); then €1 per 30 min, start paid parking in Snabb, Pargi.ee or SMS 1902. 'Convenience parking' bays by the main entrance are paid from the first minute. ERR reports children's play-area visitors can get 3-4 h free by registering with the play area. Zone shown as X9 on one part of the mall page and X122 on another, so check the sign.

name: Kristiine Centre
description: A mid-sized mall with children's clothes and toy shops and over a dozen cafés and restaurants, including BabyBack Ribs & BBQ, which has a kids' room. I couldn't confirm a public play area inside the mall.
tips: The first 2 h of parking are logged automatically by your number plate, with no disc needed.

price.note: Free entry; play centres inside are paid separately.

parkingInfo.note: First 2 h free, recorded automatically by number-plate camera. For longer stays register via SMS, the EuroPark app or Pargi.ee, zone EP395: €0.50 per 30 min, €10 per day. Lot open 07:40-23:00.

name: Järve Centre
description: A south-Tallinn mall that has the Seiklusmaa play centre, with a toddler climbing area, on its 2nd floor. Its 5 free parking hours are among the most generous in the city.
tips: Five free hours is enough for a full play session plus lunch and shopping.

price.note: Free entry; play centres inside are paid separately.

parkingInfo.note: First 5 h free; after that €0.75 per 30 min via Snabb, Pargi.ee or SMS (zone X23). Underground garage open 08:00-23:00.

name: T1 Mall of Tallinn
description: A large mall with a rooftop Ferris wheel, the SkyLab science centre and a kids' play park near the Skywheel. Super Skypark is listed separately.
tips: The 4 free parking hours can only be extended for Super Skypark customers.

price.note: Free entry; play centres inside are paid separately.

parkingInfo.note: 4 h free in the underground car park and parking garage; underground open 07:00-23:00.

name: Café Boulevard
description: A hotel café in the city centre with its own children's play area: building blocks, soft climbing steps, toys and cartoons. Parents can have a proper coffee while toddlers play close by.
tips: The café's own site and Radisson give different weekday closing times, so call if you plan an evening visit.

price.note: Pay for food; play area for café guests (no fee stated).

parkingInfo.note: City-centre street parking; check the zone sign.

name: NOP Café & Shop
description: A cosy café and organic shop in an old wooden house in Kadriorg. In summer the shady back yard has a sandbox for little ones, and it's an easy stop after Kadriorg Park or Miiamilla.
tips: Book a table by phone (+372 603 2270) on busy weekends.

price.note: Pay for food; no entry fee.

parkingInfo.note: Kadriorg street parking; zone and fees not confirmed.

name: BabyBack Ribs & BBQ (Kristiine)
address: Endla 45, Kristiine Centre, Tallinn (also Nautica, Ahtri 9, and Ülemiste)
description: An American BBQ restaurant chain whose Tallinn branches have children's playrooms, so parents can finish their meal while toddlers play. There's also a kids' menu.
tips: Ask for a table near the playroom so you can keep an eye on your toddler.

price.note: Pay for food (mains ~€10–21); no entry fee.

parkingInfo.note: First 2 h free, recorded automatically by number-plate camera. For longer stays register via SMS, the EuroPark app or Pargi.ee, zone EP395: €0.50 per 30 min, €10 per day. Lot open 07:40-23:00.

name: Lore Bistro
description: A MICHELIN Guide-recommended bistro in the Noblessner harbour area, with a children's menu, purée for the youngest and a well-stocked toy shelf. It's a grown-up meal that still works with a toddler.

price.note: Pay for food; no entry fee.

name: Mustamäe Elamus Spa
description: A large spa and pool complex with a separate toddler pool, a kids' area with slides and a 25 m sports pool. The adults-only Spa21+ is a separate zone. Babies under 2 go free, which makes it one of the best-value water trips with a toddler.
tips: Parking is free for spa visitors for 8 hours.

price.note: Elamus Spa: ages 0–1 free; ages 2–6 €6.90; full ticket €25/€32/€38 and reduced €17.90/€27/€33 depending on time; family ticket €65/€75/€92 (15% off with Perekaart). Spa21+ area is 18+ only.

parkingInfo.note: Free for spa visitors for 8 h.

name: Ring Spa & Saunas
description: A spa and sauna centre in Õismäe with several pools and a separate children's pool. Child tickets are cheap, so it's a relaxed option for parents who also want a sauna.
tips: Weekday mornings (11:00-13:00) are cheapest and quietest.

price.note: Children 0–2 free; children 3–6 €6. Adults €19 (Mon–Fri 11–15), €22 (Mon–Thu from 15), €31 (Fri evening and weekends). Family €54–72.

name: Aqua Spa (Tallink Spa & Conference Hotel)
description: A hotel water centre near the passenger port with a large indoor pool, a 30 cm deep children's pool and an outdoor pool open all year. The paddling pool is a gentle spot for toddlers.

price.note: 3-hour gift pass €20–54 (existing info); child price not confirmed.

name: Ujume Koos Baby Swimming
address: Õismäe Vaba Aja Keskus (Haabersti), Elamus Spa (Mustamäe), Nõmme ujula
description: A swim school running parent-and-baby swimming groups from 3 months old, with sessions at three Tallinn pools. Toddler groups continue after the first year.
tips: Choose the pool closest to home, since classes are weekly.

name: Garantbaby Baby & Toddler Swimming
description: Swimming classes for babies and children from 3 months to 4 years, split into a 3 months-2 years group and a 2-4 years group across several Tallinn pools.

price.note: Per lesson: trial lesson €25, private lesson €45; packages €70 / €95 (also listed €75 / €99). Parents free.

name: Kalev Spa Baby Swimming
description: Guided baby swimming sessions at the Kalev Spa water centre, from 4 months old. Passes make it easy to go weekly.

price.note: Per lesson €17 (single ticket); 10-lesson card €115 valid 90 days; €10 wristband deposit refunded. Pre-registration by e-mail.

name: Väike Päike Lasteklubi Toddler Music Group
description: A weekly 30-minute music group for children aged 10 months to 3 years, with a parent present. Toddlers play rhythm instruments and join in songs and games. The same club also runs toddler gymnastics for ages 1-2.
tips: You can pay per class (€15) to try it before committing to a month.

price.note: Per class €15, or €42 per month.

name: Loovuslaps Baby & Toddler Group
description: A group class for children aged 6 months to 3 years with an adult. A 25-30 minute lesson is followed by 15 minutes of free play.

price.note: Monthly fee: €22 (25–30 min class) or €25 (30 min music + 30 min play time).

name: MyFitness Toddler Gymnastics & Baby Swimming
description: A gym chain running parent-and-child classes: toddler gymnastics for newly walking 1-2-year-olds, ending with a circle game, and baby swimming from 3 months. Some clubs, such as Rocca al Mare, also have a kids' playroom while parents train.
tips: The MyFitness Rocca al Mare playroom costs non-members €5 per child.

price.note: Toddler gym price not shown on the price list (only general memberships).

name: Nõmme Library – toddler morning
description: Nõmme's branch library runs a monthly põnnihommik (toddler morning) with stories, play and drawing, and one listing pitches it at roughly 1.5–3-year-olds. A calm, small-group first library experience close to Nõmme station.
tips: Held on the third Wednesday of the month at 11:00 per library listings; confirm on the events calendar as listings are of mixed dates.

price.note: Free entry and free library sessions; registration may be needed when places are limited.

hours: Põnnihommik: 3rd Wednesday of the month 11:00 (unconfirmed for autumn 2026)

name: Tondi Library – Saturday toddler morning
description: Tondi library invites 2–5-year-olds with a parent to a Saturday põnnihommik of picture books, play and crafts. One of the few branches listed as running it every week rather than monthly.
tips: Listings say every Saturday at 12:00; phone 674 8647 to confirm.

price.note: Free entry and free library sessions; registration may be needed when places are limited.

name: Männiku Library – toddler morning
address: Pihlaka 12, Tallinn (4th floor of Männi community centre)
description: Männiku's library, upstairs in the Männi community centre, holds a monthly Saturday põnnihommik for 2–5-year-olds with parents. Expect picture books, simple games and a craft.
tips: Listings conflict (3rd Saturday 10:00 vs 2nd Saturday 11:00); call 655 9718 before going.

price.note: Free entry and free library sessions; registration may be needed when places are limited.

hours: Monthly Saturday põnnihommik (date/time conflicting in sources)

name: Kännukuke Library – toddler morning
description: Kännukuke, Mustamäe's children-oriented branch, welcomes toddlers with a parent to a põnnihommik on the first Saturday of the month. Sessions break over summer and resume in autumn.
tips: First Saturday of the month at 12:00 per listing; phone 683 0951 to confirm the autumn restart.

price.note: Free entry and free library sessions; registration may be needed when places are limited.

hours: Põnnihommik: 1st Saturday of the month 12:00 (summer break)

name: Sõle Library – toddler morning (Estonian/Russian)
description: Sõle library in Põhja-Tallinn has run Saturday põnnihommik sessions (11:00–12:00) for pre-schoolers with a parent, in both Estonian and Russian. Useful for Russian-speaking families too.
tips: Contact sole@tln.lib.ee / 601 9153 for the current dates.

price.note: Free entry and free library sessions; registration may be needed when places are limited.

name: Pirita Library – toddler morning (Estonian/Russian)
description: Pirita library is listed among branches holding põnnihommik sessions for 2–4-year-olds with a parent, with stories, games and drawing in Estonian and Russian. A small neighbourhood library near Pirita's forest paths.
tips: No current schedule found; check the events calendar.

price.note: Free entry and free library sessions; registration may be needed when places are limited.

name: Liivalaia Library (foreign languages) – parent & baby room
description: The foreign-language literature library has a dedicated parent-and-baby room (armchair, changing table, sink) and runs a Russian-language põnnihommik for 2–4-year-olds. A good central stop for international families looking for books in other languages.
tips: Põnnihommik places are limited and pre-registration is compulsory.

price.note: Free entry and free library sessions; registration may be needed when places are limited.

hours: Mon–Fri 10–19, Sat 10–17, Sun closed (per hours page)

name: Estonian Museum of Natural History (Old Town, closing)
description: Stuffed animals, aquariums and nature dioramas that toddlers love pointing at, in a compact Old Town building. The Lai street house closes on 31 October 2026 and the museum reopens in a new Noblessner building in 2027.
tips: Last chance until 31 Oct 2026; afterwards re-list at the Noblessner address when it opens.

price.note: Children under 8 free; pupils/students/pensioners €8; family (up to 2 adults + minor children) €24. Free for all on the last Friday of Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct.

parkingInfo.note: Zone inferred from location, not confirmed on the venue's site; check street signs. Tallinn city zones can be paid via Pargi.ee/mobile parking.

name: Fat Margaret – Estonian Maritime Museum
description: A medieval cannon tower with a medieval cog wreck, ship models and around 50 hands-on and digital stations. Fun for older toddlers who like buttons and boats, but expect towers and stairs.
tips: Children 8 and under are free, so one adult ticket plus toddler is cheap; family ticket if two adults.

price.note: Children under 8 free. Separate Fat Margaret ticket not listed; Seaplane Harbour + Fat Margaret combined ticket €30 adult / €15 child / €60 family.

parkingInfo.note: Zone inferred from location, not confirmed on the venue's site; check street signs. Tallinn city zones can be paid via Pargi.ee/mobile parking.

photos.credit: Photograph by Mike Peel (www.mikepeel.net). · CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Estonian History Museum – Maarjamäe History Centre
description: The palace museum has a hands-on children's exhibition ('I want to play!' / Children's Republic) and an outdoor playground shaped like the map of Estonia overlooking Tallinn Bay. Easy to combine with a seaside walk along Pirita tee.
tips: The Estonia-shaped playground outside is a good reward after the indoor rooms.

price.note: Children up to and including 8 free. Official ticket page lists full tickets €12–14 (plus €17), reduced €9–12 and family €24–34 across tables whose labels didn't come through in the scrape, so the Maarjamäe price can't be pinned down.

hours: Daily 10–18 (per third-party listing; check the website)

name: Tallinn City Life Museum
description: Tallinn City Museum's Old Town house tells the city's story with historic interiors and objects; better for curious older toddlers than babies. Preschoolers up to 6 enter free and the first Sunday of the month is free for everyone.
tips: Free Museum Sunday (1st Sunday) needs advance booking, with a ticket issued for every visitor including children.

price.note: Pre-school children up to 6 free; family €20 (2 adults + children under 19). Adult price not confirmed.

discounts: Free first Sunday of the month (book ahead)

parkingInfo.note: Zone inferred from location, not confirmed on the venue's site; check street signs. Tallinn city zones can be paid via Pargi.ee/mobile parking.

name: PROTO Invention Factory
description: A VR-heavy experience centre about historic inventions; mostly for older kids, but toddlers get a construction area, air cannons and curved mirrors. Under-6s are free, so it works if you are bringing older siblings.
tips: Weekday tickets are cheaper than weekends; most VR is not for toddlers.

price.note: Adult €16 Tue–Fri / €20 Sat–Sun; ages up to 18 €11; family (2 adults + minor children) €35 / €40; children up to 6 free.

parkingInfo.note: Official site has a location & parking page (prototehas.ee/en/asukoht-ja-parkimine/) – details not retrieved

name: NUKU Museum of Puppetry Arts
description: Kids can handle table, rod and hand puppets and marionettes, and short plays or storytimes sometimes run during the day. Under-3s free, but the museum is not stroller-accessible.
tips: Leave the stroller near the main entrance; reduced and family tickets only at the box office.

price.note: Under-3s free; older child price not confirmed. Family = up to 2 adults + at least 1 child under 16.

discounts: Free with Tallinn Card (per Visit Tallinn)

parkingInfo.note: Zone inferred from location, not confirmed on the venue's site; check street signs. Tallinn city zones can be paid via Pargi.ee/mobile parking.

name: NUKU Theatre (Estonian Youth Theatre) – toddler shows
description: The national puppet/youth theatre stages short (30–45 min) shows for small children in its intimate Oval Hall, e.g. 'Minu jälg' (3+). A baby piece 'Nutude salajutud' for 10 months–2 years ran until March 2026, so watch for new baby productions.
tips: Filter the playbill for 'väikelapsele' (for small children); most current titles are 3+.

price.note: Per show: performances for young children and preschoolers €13 per ticket (Piletilevi service fee €1.90). Group of 10 children gets one free adult ticket.

parkingInfo.note: Zone inferred from location, not confirmed on the venue's site; check street signs. Tallinn city zones can be paid via Pargi.ee/mobile parking.

photos.credit: National Archives of Estonia · No restrictions

name: Estonian National Opera – Concert for the Littlest
address: Estonia pst 4, Tallinn (Estonia restaurant, entry via theatre foyer)
description: A ~45-minute classical concert for 0–3-year-olds where babies crawl on a big themed play mat and parents can lie down and listen. Strollers stay in the lobby and there is a café and changing table.
tips: Sessions (e.g. 10:00 and 11:30) sell out; check tickets.opera.ee and Fienta for new dates.

price.note: Sources conflict: €15 standard / €10 reduced, or €6–10; child under 3 on reduced ticket – verify when booking.

parkingInfo.note: Zone inferred from location, not confirmed on the venue's site; check street signs. Tallinn city zones can be paid via Pargi.ee/mobile parking.

name: Apollo Kino Mustamäe – Mum & Baby cinema day
nameLocal: Apollo Kino – Emme ja beebi kinopäev
description: Periodic weekday-morning screenings of regular films for parents with babies, with dimmed-but-not-dark lights, quieter sound, stroller parking and a changing table. Best for pre-walkers; busy toddlers may find it hard.
tips: Kids under 3 need no ticket and seats are sold with a free seat beside you; no reservations, buy online or at the box office.

price.note: One adult ticket; children under 3 free. Adult price not confirmed.

hours: Occasional Tuesday mornings – check the website

parkingInfo.note: Shopping-centre parking; cost not verified

name: Tondiraba Park
description: A 29-hectare park with what Visit Tallinn calls the largest sports-field and playground complex in the Baltics, with playgrounds for different ages. Wide paved paths make it easy with a stroller or balance bike.
tips: Visitor reviews mention a coffee spot on site; head for the smaller-kid play zones as the big structures suit older children.

price.note: Free public playground.

parkingInfo.note: Free parking listed by Visit Harju; unconfirmed by the city.

transport: Bus stops Tähesaju tee, Kurina, Linnamäe tee

name: Pae Park (Perepark family area)
address: Paepargi, Lasnamäe, Tallinn (sources give Paepargi 21 or 37)
description: A former limestone quarry turned modern park around a lake with a red suspension bridge; its 'Perepark' (family park) section has many playgrounds and sports courts. Good for a lakeside stroller loop plus playground stop.
tips: There is a 1.8 km paved circuit around the park — easy for strollers.

price.note: Free public park/promenade.

transport: Bus stops Kumu (~365 m) and Kiive (~425 m)

name: Paasiku family playground
description: A small neighbourhood family playground in Lasnamäe that is well rated by locals and packed with play equipment and sports facilities. Handy if you live nearby; not a destination in itself.

price.note: Free public playground.

name: Police Park playgrounds
address: Politseiaed, between Pronksi, Gonsiori, F. R. Kreutzwaldi and J. Kunderi streets, Tallinn
description: Central city park next to the Hilton with playgrounds for children of all ages, a fountain, skate park and dog area. A convenient green break when you are in the city centre with a toddler.
tips: Toddlers may want to steer clear of the skate park side when it's busy.

price.note: Free public playground.

parkingInfo.note: Surrounding streets are in a central paid zone (likely Kesklinn) — check street signs. Tallinn has 4 paid street zones (Kesklinn, Südalinn, Vanalinn, Pirita); first 15 min free with parking clock.

photos.credit: North Charleston from North Charleston, SC, United States · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Tammsaare Park playground
address: Tammsaare park, Estonia pst side (between Estonia pst and the pavilion), Tallinn
description: A city-centre playground on the Estonia Theatre side of Tammsaare Park, planned with musical instruments (bongo drums, xylophone), a slide and trampolines. Easy to combine with errands in the centre.

price.note: Free public playground.

parkingInfo.note: City-centre paid zone (likely Südalinn) and nearby malls' paid garages. Tallinn has 4 paid street zones (Kesklinn, Südalinn, Vanalinn, Pirita); first 15 min free with parking clock.

transport: Viru / Estonia stops (many tram and bus lines)

name: Cruise Terminal rooftop promenade
address: Old City Harbour, Tallinn Cruise Terminal (northwest pier), Tallinn
description: An 850 m public promenade across the roof of the cruise terminal with sea views, seating, a children's playground and a small sports area. A breezy, car-free walk with a toddler, linking to the seafront Culture Kilometre.
tips: Bikes, scooters and skateboards are not allowed on the promenade; bring a windproof layer.

price.note: Free public rooftop promenade and playground.

name: Reidi tee seaside promenade
address: Reidi tee, from Lootsi/Ahtri junction to the Russalka monument, Tallinn
description: A ~2 km seaside walking and cycling route on smooth asphalt with benches and eight playgrounds along the way. Perfect for a stroller walk with regular playground stops.
tips: Continue past Russalka onto the Pirita promenade if the little one naps.

price.note: Free public park/promenade.

name: Pirita Promenade
address: Pirita tee, from the Russalka monument to Pirita beach, Tallinn
description: A long seaside path (about 4 km from Russalka to the Pirita river mouth) with separate pedestrian and cycling lanes, sea views and several playgrounds and sports fields along the way. Great for long stroller walks.
tips: Can be very windy — a stroller rain/wind cover helps.

price.note: Free public park/promenade.

parkingInfo.operator: Tallinn city (Pirita zone) near the beach end
parkingInfo.note: Pirita zone (car parks at Merivälja tee 1c and 1e) is paid 15 May–15 Sept, 10:00–22:00, €0.01/min; first 15 min free with parking clock.

name: Lepistiku Park
description: A lit nature-conservation park in the middle of Mustamäe with ponds, a children's playground, sports courts and a pedestrian bridge. A calm, local spot for duck-watching and a playground run.

price.note: Free public park/promenade.

name: Männi Park
description: One of Mustamäe's largest pine parks, with a children's playground, a stony picnic area and a bandstand. In winter the city sets up an outdoor ice rink here.

price.note: Free public park/promenade.

name: Duck Pond Park
description: A nearly six-hectare park around a pond with resident mallards, a lit fountain, paths, benches and children's playgrounds. Duck-spotting plus a playground makes an easy toddler outing.

price.note: Free public park/promenade.

name: Õismäe Pond Park
description: A 9-hectare park ringing the round Õismäe pond, with a family playground, a children's traffic circle, a fitness path and paved loops. A flat, stroller-friendly circuit popular with local families.
tips: The children's traffic circle is great for balance bikes and trikes.

price.note: Free public park/promenade.

name: Kopli Birch Park
description: A protected forest park in Kopli, refurbished in 2021, with winding lit paths, a children's playground, swings, picnic spots and benches. A shady forest walk reachable by tram.

price.note: Free public park/promenade.

name: Putukaväil green corridor (Põhja-Tallinn section)
address: Former power-line corridor between Sõle street and Stroomi beach, Tallinn
description: A new green corridor (part of Tallinn's 14 km Putukaväil 'Bug Trail') with play and sports areas between Sõle street and Stroomi beach. In 2025 ERR reported that its play equipment and toilets were closed pending a usage permit, so check status before going.
tips: Check recent news or the Põhja-Tallinn district before a dedicated trip.

price.note: Free public park/promenade.

name: Paljassaare nature reserve boardwalk
address: Paljassaare peninsula, near Pikakari beach, Tallinn
description: A 550 m boardwalk (two sections) through the Paljassaare conservation area, where over 220 bird species have been recorded and Highland cattle graze in summer. Toddlers love spotting the cows and birds.
tips: Bus 59 to the Pikakari terminus; paths beyond the boardwalk are unpaved.

price.note: Free nature trail.

name: Pikakari Beach
description: A Blue Flag sandy beach on the Paljassaare peninsula with swings, a children's playground, a boardwalk and outdoor toilets. Note that the water gets deep quickly, so it is better for sand play than paddling.
tips: Keep toddlers close at the waterline — the sea deepens fast here.

price.note: Free public beach.

name: Räägu Park
address: Nõmme tee 52 (corner of Nõmme and Räägu streets), Tallinn
description: A one-hectare neighbourhood park with several playgrounds and a basketball court, designed for all ages. A handy local stop in the Nõmme/Mustamäe border area.

price.note: Free public playground.

name: Glehn Park
description: A forested hillside park around Baron von Glehn's 19th-century castle, dotted with unusual sculptures that make a fun 'spot the statue' walk for toddlers. Paths are hilly and partly unpaved.
tips: A sturdy all-terrain stroller or carrier works better than a city stroller on the slopes.

price.note: Free public park/promenade.

name: Pääsküla Bog nature trail
description: A real bog inside city limits: a 4 km trail of dirt paths and boardwalks, plus a separate 2 km children's/accessible route that mainly runs on paved paths and is fully passable with a stroller. A 10 m observation tower sits in the Männiku area.
tips: Stick to the 2 km children's loop with a stroller; the 280 m floating boardwalk on the long loop isn't stroller-friendly.

price.note: Free nature trail.

name: Harku Lake Beach
description: Tallinn's only lakeside beach, with children's playgrounds, changing cabins, a shower and ball-game areas. The lake warms up early, so it's one of the first places to paddle in late spring.
tips: Lifeguards only June–August.

price.note: Free public beach.

parkingInfo.note: Free parking area near the beach plus bicycle parking.

name: Kakumäe Beach
description: A sandy, usually calm beach with relatively shallow water that the official listings call suitable for families with children. Has playgrounds, ball courts, changing cabins, a shower and an ice-cream stand.
tips: Arrive early on hot days; parking is free but unguarded.

price.note: Free public beach.

hours: Open all year; lifeguards 1 Jun–31 Aug 9:00–20:00

parkingInfo.note: Free unguarded car and bicycle parking.

transport: Bus 21 to Kakumäe tee, or 21A/21B to Sooranna tee

name: Old Town ice rink (Harju street)
address: Harju tn, next to St Nicholas' (Niguliste) Church, Tallinn
description: Tallinn's atmospheric open-air rink at the edge of the Old Town, usually open from late November to the end of March. Little ones can toddle on the ice or watch from the side, especially pretty under the evening lights.
tips: Under-3s have skated free in past seasons; bring a helmet and waterproof mittens.

price.note: Per hour (2025/26 city-rink prices): €6.90–10.90, children/seniors €4.70–8.80; skate rental €5. Under-3s free (2024 reports). 2026/27 prices not yet published.

discounts: Season passes valid at all city rinks
hours: Seasonal (approx. late Nov–end of March), daily approx. 10:00–22:00; check the website

parkingInfo.note: Old Town street parking is expensive and paid 24 h; use public transport if you can.

name: Männi Park outdoor ice rink
description: One of Tallinn's city-run outdoor rinks, set up in Männi Park and typically opening earlier (late October/November) than the Old Town rink. A less crowded place for a first wobble on skates.

price.note: Per hour (2025/26 city-rink prices): €6.90–10.90, discounted (children/seniors) €4.70–8.80. An older ERR article quoted €6.30–9.50/hour. 2026/27 prices not yet published.

name: Song Festival Grounds sledding & snow tubing
description: The long, gentle slope of the Song Festival Grounds is Tallinn's classic sledding hill, with snow-tubing tracks and equipment rental when snow allows. Great for toddler sledging with a parent, though it can get crowded.
tips: Go early on snowy weekend mornings and stick to the gentler edges away from fast sledders.

price.note: Sledding on the open slope is free; snowtubing/rental is paid (prices not confirmed).

hours: Listed 1 Dec–15 Mar, depending on snow

name: Nõmme forest-park sledding slopes
address: Park forest between Nõmme and Mustamäe, near Nõmme market, Tallinn
description: The hilly Nõmme-Mustamäe forest park near Nõmme market is a favourite free sledding area. Some slopes are steep and nothing is supervised, so pick a gentle run for toddlers.
tips: Bring your own sled; guides warn some Nõmme hills are dangerously steep.

price.note: Free sledding hill.

name: Nõmme Sports Centre ski trails
description: Lit, maintained cross-country trails (1–15 km loops, including an artificial-snow loop) connected by tunnel to the Harku forest trails. Toddlers can ride in a ski pulk/sled while a parent skis, or try their first steps on mini skis.
tips: The 5 km loop is reported lit all night; ski rental is available on site (child sizes unconfirmed).

price.note: Trails free to use; ski rental paid.

hours: Centre Mon–Sat 08:00–22:00, Sun 09:00–22:00; trails depend on snow

name: Tallinn Christmas Market
description: The festive market on Town Hall Square with a big Christmas tree, stalls and lights. For toddlers the tree, lights and carousel-style atmosphere are the draw; go early in the day to avoid evening crowds.
tips: Cobbles are bumpy — a carrier is easier than a stroller.

price.note: Free entry; pay for rides, food and stalls.

hours: Seasonal; 2026/27 reported as 20 Nov–6 Jan, daily at least 12:00–20:00

parkingInfo.note: Old Town parking is paid 24 h and limited.

name: Keila-Joa waterfall & park (RMK)
description: A riverside manor park with the Keila waterfall, footbridges and a 2.1 km nature trail, about 30–40 minutes' drive west of Tallinn. Only the first 250 m are stroller/wheelchair accessible, and stairs lead down to the falls.
tips: Bring a baby carrier for the stairs down to the waterfall.

price.note: Park free; Keila-Joa Castle has separate paid entry.

parkingInfo.note: RMK lot for ~20 cars at trail start; fee not stated (RMK sites are typically free).

name: Jägala Waterfall
description: Estonia's widest natural waterfall, about 25 km (≈30 min) east of Tallinn, reached by a short walk from the car park on gravel paths. Toddlers love the roar; in cold winters it freezes into ice curtains.
tips: The riverbank is unfenced in places — keep toddlers in hand or carrier near the edge.

price.note: Free to visit.

parkingInfo.note: Large car park on site; fee not confirmed; no toilet.

name: Viru Bog boardwalk (Lahemaa)
address: Viru raba parking, Lahemaa National Park (off Tallinn–Narva highway)
description: RMK's famous bog boardwalk; the first 1.3 km to the observation tower is built to suit wheelchairs and prams (with a ramp to the tower's first platform). Roughly 45–50 minutes' drive from Tallinn, so it's at the edge of a toddler day trip.
tips: After the tower ramp the boardwalk narrows — turn back at the tower with a stroller; very busy on summer weekends.

price.note: Free RMK nature trail.

parkingInfo.note: New RMK parking lot at trail start; gravel access road may be unfinished.

name: Polli Farm Zoo (Tuhala)
address: Polli farm, Kata küla, Kose vald (near Tuhala Witch's Well)
description: A small farm zoo where children can see and pet animals and birds, visit the barn and stables, and ride a pony. Combine it with the nearby Tuhala Witch's Well (Nõiakaev).
tips: Bring cabbage, carrots or bird seed to feed the animals; call ahead for hours.

price.note: Prices not confirmed.

name: Kallaste Farm 'Elamustalu' family activity centre
description: A tourist farm about 45 minutes southwest of Tallinn with pygmy goats, rabbits, chickens and geese to meet and feed, plus a playground with an old bus to explore and a trampoline. Near Rummu lake.
tips: The animal park is by advance booking only.

price.note: Prices not confirmed.

hours: Listed daily 10:00–19:00, all year (animal park by booking)

name: Laulasmaa beach
description: A sandy-bottomed seaside beach backed by pine forest, about 40 km west of Tallinn, and the start of the 7 km Laulasmaa–Lohusalu shore trail. Sand play and pine-forest picnics make an easy summer day out.
tips: You can walk just a short stretch of the shore trail and turn back.

price.note: Free public beach.
